mainTopic: The מסית and the rule of hidden witnesses, the מדיח, and the מכשף: who counts as one and how he is put to death.
overview: The amud opens with the last words of an earlier discussion: a פסוק was quoted only as a memory sign. Then a משנה describes the מסית, an ordinary person who tries to pull another person into עבודה זרה. It teaches that only for him may בית דין hide witnesses to catch him, and it explains how that trap works. The גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה follows. רבי שמעון seems to fit the beginning and the רבנן seem to fit the end. רבינא and רב פפא each show how the whole משנה can follow the רבנן. A ברייתא describes the hidden-witness setup in detail and tells of בן סטדא in לוד, and the גמרא explains his name. A new משנה then defines the מדיח and the מכשף, who is liable only for real sorcery, not for tricking the eyes. The גמרא teaches that מכשפה includes men and women. רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא then argue whether a sorcerer is killed by the sword or by stoning, and their debate continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse is only a memory sign
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the previous discussion by saying the פסוק it quoted was not a real source for the הלכה, only a sign to help remember it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just a sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the earlier discussion. It explains that a פסוק quoted there was only a helpful reminder, not a real proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier question was why a פסוק was brought if the הלכה did not depend on it. The answer is that it works as a סימן, a memory hook. Just as the law of the נערה המאורסה deals with her first relations, the law of a בת כהן who sinned deals with her first disqualification from כהונה.

phrases.english: It is merely a sign.
phrases.notes: This answers the earlier question about why a פסוק was quoted. It wasn't a real source, just a reminder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous discussion before the new משנה begins.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifies the quoted פסוק as a memory sign instead of a legal source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק was being used as a real source for the הלכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is only a סימן and the הלכה does not depend on it.

steps.title: Who the inciter is and what he says
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines the מסית as an ordinary person who tries to persuade another ordinary person to worship an idol, and it quotes the kind of thing he says.
steps.simpleTranslation: The inciter is an ordinary person, and he incites an ordinary person. He says: there is an idol in such-and-such a place. This is how it eats, this is how it drinks, this is how it does good, this is how it does harm.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains who counts as a מסית and gives an example of his persuasion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה limits the case on both sides. The inciter is a הדיוט, not a נביא, and the person he persuades is a single הדיוט, not a whole crowd or city. His pitch makes the idol sound alive and powerful: it eats, it drinks, it rewards and it punishes.

keyTerms.meaning: One who persuades another to worship idols
An ordinary person, not a נביא
Literally 'a fear'; here, an object of worship (an idol)

steps.confusionAlert: The word הדיוט appears twice. The first describes the inciter (he is not a נביא), and the second describes the person he persuades (one individual, not a crowd).

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The inciter: this is an ordinary person,
and one who incites an ordinary person.
He said: There is an idol in such-and-such a place,
phrases.notes: Literally 'a fear.' It means something people fear and worship, an idol.

phrases.english: this is how it eats, this is how it drinks,
this is how it does good, this is how it does harm.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמֵּסִית – זֶה הֶדְיוֹט, וְהַמֵּסִית אֶת הַהֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מסית is an ordinary person who persuades an individual to worship an idol, for example by describing its power.

steps.title: Only for the inciter may witnesses be hidden
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a general rule: for every other death-penalty sin, בית דין does not hide witnesses to trap the sinner. The מסית is the one exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: For everyone liable to death in the Torah, we do not hide witnesses to catch them, except for this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states a general principle about trapping sinners and names the מסית as its single exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally בית דין does not set up hidden witnesses to catch someone. The מסית is treated differently and may be trapped this way. The next step explains how the trap works in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: People liable to the death penalty
Hide or set an ambush (of witnesses)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main הלכה that sets the מסית apart from every other capital case, and the rest of the משנה builds on it.

phrases.english: All those liable to death penalties in the Torah,
we do not hide witnesses against them,
except for this one.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל חַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת שֶׁבְּתוֹרָה, אֵין מַכְמִינִין עֲלֵיהֶם, חוּץ מִזּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a special procedural rule for the מסית defined in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hidden witnesses may be used only against a מסית, not against any other person liable to death.

steps.title: How the inciter is caught
steps.stepSummary: If the מסית spoke to two people, they serve as witnesses and he is stoned. If he spoke to one, that person says he has interested friends so that more witnesses can hear.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said it to two people, they are his witnesses: they bring him to court and stone him. If he said it to one person, that person says, 'I have friends who want this.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains how the special trapping rule works, depending on whether the מסית spoke to two people or to one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people are already enough witnesses, so the case goes straight to בית דין and he receives סקילה. One witness is not enough, so the listener draws the מסית into repeating his words before others. That is how the 'hiding witnesses' rule from step 3 is carried out.
steps.whatToRemember: The מסית is an ordinary person persuading an individual. He is the only capital sinner against whom hidden witnesses are allowed: two listeners are enough to testify, and a single listener draws him out in front of more witnesses.

phrases.english: If he said it to two, they are his witnesses,
and they bring him to court
and they stone him.
If he said it to one, he says:
phrases.notes: 'He' here is the person being persuaded, speaking to the מסית.

phrases.english: "I have friends who are interested in this."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the exception in step 3 is put into practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two listeners serve as witnesses for stoning. A single listener draws the מסית out in front of more witnesses.

steps.title: Catching a cunning מסית with hidden witnesses
steps.stepSummary: If the מסית is too careful to speak in front of two people, בית דין hides witnesses behind a fence. If he repeats his persuasion and refuses to back down, he is brought to בית דין and stoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the מסית is cunning and won't speak in front of two people, witnesses are hidden behind a fence. The man he tried to persuade says, 'Repeat what you told me in private,' and he does. The man answers, 'How can we leave our God in heaven and worship wood and stones?' If the מסית takes it back, good. If he says, 'This is our duty, this is good for us,' the hidden witnesses bring him to בית דין and he is stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues from Step 4. It explains how witnesses are set up when the מסית is too careful to talk in front of more than one person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the exception from Step 3 put into practice: hidden witnesses are allowed only for a מסית. Even so, the man first argues against idol worship. This gives the מסית one more chance to back down before he is punished.

keyTerms.meaning: Cunning, careful (here: he makes sure not to speak in front of witnesses)
In private, when the two were alone

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how seriously the Torah treats the מסית. Even the normal rule against trapping a sinner is set aside for him, yet he is still given a chance to back down.

phrases.english: If he was cunning
and he cannot speak in front of them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the two or more people. He is careful never to say it in front of enough witnesses.

phrases.english: they hide witnesses for him behind the fence.
And he says to him:
phrases.notes: "He" is the man the מסית tried to persuade; "him" is the מסית.

phrases.english: "Say what you said in private!"
And the other one says it to him.
And he says to him:
"How can we leave our God who is in heaven
and go and worship wood and stones?"

phrases.aramaic: אִם חוֹזֵר בּוֹ – הֲרֵי זֶה מוּטָב,
phrases.english: If he takes it back, that is good,
but if he said:
"This is our duty, this is good for us,"
those standing behind the fence

phrases.aramaic: מְבִיאִין אוֹתוֹ לְבֵית דִּין וְסוֹקְלִין אוֹתוֹ.
phrases.english: bring him to court and stone him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם הָיָה עָרוּם וְאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְדַבֵּר בִּפְנֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues Step 4 by covering the case where the מסית refuses to speak in front of two people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses may be hidden behind a fence to catch a cunning מסית. If he does not take back his words, he is brought to בית דין and stoned.

steps.title: Which statements count as persuading
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists statements that count: 'I will' / 'I will go and' / 'Let us go and' worship, sacrifice, burn incense, pour a libation, or bow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who says: 'I will worship,' 'I will go and worship,' 'Let us go and worship'; 'I will sacrifice,' 'I will go and sacrifice,' 'Let us go and sacrifice'; 'I will burn incense,' 'I will go and burn incense,' 'Let us go and burn incense'; 'I will pour a libation,' 'I will go and pour,' 'Let us go and pour'; 'I will bow,' 'I will go and bow,' 'Let us go and bow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a list of sentences that make a person a מסית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list covers the main ways of serving an idol: general worship, sacrificing, burning incense, pouring a libation, and bowing. Each one appears in three forms: 'I will,' 'I will go and,' and 'Let us go and.' So even saying 'I will do it' to someone, without asking him to join, can count as persuasion.

keyTerms.meaning: I will pour a libation (wine poured as an offering)

steps.confusionAlert: Even 'I will worship' counts, though the speaker never directly says 'come with me.' Don't assume only 'let us go' counts.

phrases.english: One who says: "I will worship,"
"I will go and worship," "Let us go and worship";
"I will sacrifice," "I will go and sacrifice," "Let us go and sacrifice";
"I will burn incense," "I will go and burn incense," "Let us go and burn incense";
"I will pour a libation," "I will go and pour," "Let us go and pour";
"I will bow," "I will go and bow," "Let us go and bow."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה by listing the exact wordings that make someone a מסית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'I will,' 'I will go and,' or 'Let us go and' worship, sacrifice, burn incense, pour a libation, or bow counts as persuading.

steps.title: Reading the משנה closely: a נביא or a crowd gets חנק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה's words closely. 'The מסית is an ordinary person' suggests a נביא who persuades gets חנק. 'Who persuades an ordinary person' suggests that persuading many people gets חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The מסית is an ordinary person.' The reason he is stoned is that he is ordinary, which suggests a נביא gets חנק. It also said: 'who persuades an ordinary person.' The reason is that he persuaded one person, which suggests persuading many people gets חנק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It draws two conclusions from the exact words of the משנה (from Step 2), and this sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each detail in the משנה is read as a limit. The מסית gets סקילה only because he is an ordinary person persuading one person. That suggests a נביא, or someone who persuades a crowd (like the people who lead an עיר הנדחת astray), gets the lighter death, חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is... (used to start an inference)
But then... (what follows from the opposite case)
Strangulation, a lighter death penalty than סקילה

phrases.english: GEMARA: "The מסית: this is an ordinary person."
The reason is that he is an ordinary person,
but a prophet would be by strangulation.
"And who persuades an ordinary person":
the reason is that it is one individual,
but many people would be by strangulation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the opening words of the משנה (Step 2) and draws conclusions from them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's wording suggests that a נביא who persuades, or someone who persuades many people, is put to death by חנק rather than סקילה.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: Based on those conclusions, the גמרא asks which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא would agree with the conclusions it just drew. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The conclusions in Step 7 are not obvious, because some hold that a נביא who persuades is stoned. So the גמרא wants to know who the משנה is following.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is our mishna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the conclusions drawn in Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a נביא, or someone who persuades many, gets חנק, matching the משנה's wording.

steps.title: It is רבי שמעון, as the ברייתא shows
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי שמעון. A ברייתא shows that he holds a נביא who leads people astray, and the people who lead an עיר הנדחת astray, get חנק, while the תנא קמא says סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי שמעון, as a ברייתא teaches: a נביא who led people astray is stoned; רבי שמעון says by strangulation. Those who led an עיר הנדחת astray are stoned; רבי שמעון says by strangulation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי שמעון, and brings a ברייתא as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the first opinion gives סקילה both to a נביא and to those who lead a whole city astray. רבי שמעון gives חנק in both cases. These are the same two conclusions drawn from the משנה in Step 7, so the משנה matches רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Those who lead a city astray so that it becomes an עיר הנדחת

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה follows רבי שמעון. An ordinary person who persuades one person gets סקילה. A נביא, or those who lead a whole city astray, get חנק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the משנה limits stoning to an ordinary person persuading one person: the other cases get חנק according to רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Shimon,
as it was taught:
A prophet who led people astray is by stoning.
Rabbi Shimon says: By strangulation.
Those who lead astray a city that goes astray are by stoning.
phrases.notes: This is the city where most people were led to idol worship (דברים 13:13–19).

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: By strangulation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי שמעון, who holds in a ברייתא that a נביא who leads astray, and those who lead an עיר הנדחת astray, get חנק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבי שמעון disagrees with the first opinion and gives חנק in both cases.

steps.title: The end of the משנה seems to follow the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה gives סקילה to the מדיח, who according to רב is someone who leads a whole city astray. That fits רבנן, not רבי שמעון. Can the משנה really switch opinions halfway through?
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the last part of the משנה: 'The מדיח is the one who says, Let us go and worship idols.' רב יהודה said in the name of רב that this is about people who lead an עיר הנדחת astray. The משנה gives them סקילה, so this part follows רבנן. Can it be that the first part follows רבי שמעון and the last part follows רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If the start of the משנה follows רבי שמעון, the end of the משנה seems to follow רבנן instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 we learned that רבי שמעון gives חנק to people who lead a city astray, while the תנא קמא gives them סקילה. The end of our משנה lists the מדיח among those who get סקילה, and רב says the מדיח leads a whole city astray. So the end follows רבנן, and it is very unlikely that one משנה switches opinions in the middle.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the last part (of the משנה); it opens a challenge from the end of the text
One who leads people astray to idol worship, especially a whole city
The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
We have arrived at the view of the רבנן

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the מסית with the מדיח. The מסית persuades individuals. The מדיח, as רב explains here, leads a whole city astray.

phrases.english: Say the last part:
The one who leads astray is the one who says,
"Let us go and worship idols."
And רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
They taught this about those who lead a city astray.
So now we have arrived at the view of the רבנן.
Is the first part רבי שמעון and the last part the רבנן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 9 that the משנה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the משנה gives סקילה to people who lead a city astray, which is the view of רבנן. A single משנה should not switch from רבי שמעון to רבנן.

steps.title: רבינא: the whole משנה follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the whole משנה is רבנן. Its wording follows a 'not only this, but even that' style.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The whole משנה follows the רבנן. It is teaching in a 'not only this, but even that' style.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge by saying the משנה never followed רבי שמעון at all. The whole משנה follows רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words in the משנה were read in step 7 as leaving out cases that get חנק. רבינא reads them another way: the משנה teaches the simpler case first and then adds a bigger one. Not only does someone who persuades one person get סקילה, but even someone who leads a whole city astray gets סקילה. So the משנה does not split between two opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: The whole (משנה) is the view of the רבנן
Not only this, but even that; a teaching style that adds a bigger case after a smaller one

phrases.english: רבינא said:
The whole of it follows the רבנן,
and it is teaching: not only this, but even that.
phrases.notes: Not only does someone who persuades a single person get סקילה, but even someone who misleads a whole city does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by giving up on the idea that the משנה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה's wording so that the whole משנה follows one opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra words in the משנה were meant to leave out cases that get חנק, which would match רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבנן throughout. Its wording builds from a smaller case to a bigger one rather than leaving cases out.

steps.title: רב פפא: 'an ordinary person' is about hiding witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the words 'the מסית is a הדיוט' do not leave out a נביא. They teach that we may hide witnesses to catch him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: When the משנה teaches 'the מסית is a הדיוט,' it is talking about hiding witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different way to keep the whole משנה with רבנן. He explains what the word הדיוט is really teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7 the גמרא read הדיוט as 'an ordinary person, not a נביא,' which pointed to רבי שמעון. רב פפא says the word is not about who the מסית is. It tells us how he is treated: like a lowly person whom we may trap by hiding witnesses, as we saw in step 5. So nothing in the משנה requires the view of רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Hiding witnesses in ambush to catch the מסית

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the hidden-witness rule from step 5 is written into the very definition of the מסית.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
When it teaches, "The מסית is an ordinary person,"
it is about hiding witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: כִּי קָתָנֵי מֵסִית זֶה הֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge of step 10, different from רבינא's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving a word a different meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הדיוט means 'not a נביא,' so a נביא who persuades would get חנק, which is רבי שמעון's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: הדיוט means he is treated as lowly and may be trapped with hidden witnesses. It does not leave out a נביא.

steps.title: A ברייתא: we hide witnesses only for the מסית
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that for every other death-penalty sin we do not hide witnesses. The only exception is the מסית.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: For all the other people the תורה puts to death, we do not hide witnesses to catch them, except for this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רב פפא. It shows that hiding witnesses is a special rule just for the מסית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since hiding witnesses is used only for the מסית, it makes sense that the משנה would point to it when describing him. That backs up רב פפא's reading of הדיוט. The מסית is singled out for harsh treatment.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are liable to the death penalty

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to keep the whole משנה with רבנן. רבינא says the משנה uses a 'not only this, but even that' style. רב פפא says הדיוט refers to hiding witnesses, which we do only for the מסית.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: וּשְׁאָר כׇּל חַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: And all the others in the Torah who are liable to death,
we do not hide witnesses against them,
except for this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support רב פפא's answer.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that הדיוט refers to hiding witnesses
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא teaching that witnesses are hidden only for the מסית

steps.title: How the hidden witnesses are set up
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains exactly how the court catches a מסית with hidden witnesses. If he does not take back his words, he is brought to court and stoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is it done? They light a candle for him in an inner room, and they seat witnesses in an outer room. That way the witnesses can see him and hear him, but he cannot see them. The person he tried to pull away says: 'Say again what you told me in private.' He says it. The person answers: 'How can we leave our God in Heaven and worship idols?' If he takes it back, good. But if he says, 'This is our duty and this is good for us,' the witnesses listening outside bring him to court, and he is stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 13 keeps going. It gives the practical steps for hiding witnesses to catch a מסית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said that only for a מסית do we hide witnesses. Now we see how it works. The light is on him and the witnesses are in the dark, so they can see and hear him without him knowing. He is also given a chance to take back his words before he is punished.

keyTerms.meaning: They light a lamp for him, so the witnesses can see him
The inner room, where the מסית sits in the light
The outer room, where the witnesses hide
In private, just the two of them

steps.whatToRemember: A מסית is the one case where the court sets a trap with hidden witnesses. Even so, he gets a chance to take back his words first.

phrases.english: How do they do this to him?

phrases.aramaic: מַדְלִיקִין לוֹ אֶת הַנֵּר בַּבַּיִת הַפְּנִימִי,
phrases.english: They light a candle for him in the inner room,
and they seat witnesses for him in the outer room,
so that they can see him

phrases.aramaic: וְשׁוֹמְעִין אֶת קוֹלוֹ, וְהוּא אֵינוֹ רוֹאֶה אוֹתָן.
phrases.english: and hear his voice, but he cannot see them.
And the other one says to him:
phrases.notes: The 'other one' is the person the מסית tried to pull toward idol worship.

phrases.english: "Say what you told me in private,"
and he says it to him.
And the other one says to him:
"How can we leave our God in Heaven
and worship idols?"
If he takes it back, good.
But if he says: "This is our duty
and this is good for us,"
the witnesses who are listening from outside

phrases.aramaic: מְבִיאִין אוֹתוֹ לְבֵית דִּין וְסוֹקְלִין אוֹתוֹ.
phrases.english: bring him to court, and they stone him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 13 and spells out how the hiding of witnesses works.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses hide in a dark outer room while the מסית sits lit in an inner room. If he repeats his call to idol worship and does not take it back, they testify and he is stoned.

steps.title: A real case: בן סטדא in לוד
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tells of a real case where this method was used on a man called בן סטדא in לוד, who was hanged on ערב פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what they did to בן סטדא in לוד, and they hanged him on ערב פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a real example of the hidden-witness method being used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the procedure from step 14 was actually carried out, not just a theory. The name בן סטדא will raise a question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of the man caught this way

phrases.english: And so they did to בן סטדא in לוד,
and they hanged him on the eve of פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life example of the procedure in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The hidden-witness method was actually used on בן סטדא in לוד.

steps.title: Why is he called בן סטדא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why he is called בן סטדא, when he was known as בן פנדירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן סטדא? He was the son of פנדירא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the name in the ברייתא does not match the name he was known by, and asks about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone can only be 'the son of' one father. So if he was בן פנדירא, why call him בן סטדא? The next steps try to explain the two names.

keyTerms.meaning: The other name he was known by

phrases.english: בן סטדא?
He was the son of פנדירא!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the name used in the story in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The name בן סטדא in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He was known as בן פנדירא, so calling him בן סטדא seems to contradict that.

steps.title: רב חסדא: two different men
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא suggests that סטדא was the mother's husband and פנדירא was the man she had a relationship with.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The husband was סטדא, and the man who was with her was פנדירא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא tries to explain both names by saying they belong to two different men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He was called after סטדא because that was his mother's husband. But his real father was פנדירא. This way both names fit.

keyTerms.meaning: The man who had relations with her (not her husband)

phrases.english: רב חסדא said:
The husband was סטדא; the man who had relations with her was פנדירא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בַּעַל סָטָדָא, בּוֹעֵל פַּנְדִּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two names between two different people
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both names seemed to be the name of his father, which cannot be.
steps.terutzMaskana: סטדא was the mother's husband; פנדירא was the real father.

steps.title: But the husband was פפוס בן יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the mother's husband was פפוס בן יהודה, not סטדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The husband? The husband was פפוס בן יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב חסדא's answer, because the husband's name is known and it was not סטדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא needed the husband to be named סטדא. But the husband was known as פפוס בן יהודה, so that answer does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of the mother's husband

phrases.english: The husband?
He was פפוס בן יהודה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's answer in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the husband was named סטדא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The husband's known name was פפוס בן יהודה, so סטדא cannot be the husband.

steps.title: Maybe סטדא was his mother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests instead that סטדא was his mother's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, his mother was סטדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new answer: he was named after his mother, סטדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband was not סטדא, maybe the mother was. Then 'בן סטדא' means 'son of his mother סטדא', and פנדירא can still be his father.

phrases.english: Rather, his mother was סטדא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: סטדא was thought to be the husband.

steps.title: But his mother was מרים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back again: his mother was מרים, who braided women's hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: His mother? His mother was מרים, the one who braided women's hair!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the new answer too, because the mother's name is known and it was מרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once again a known name gets in the way. If his mother was called מרים, then סטדא cannot be her name.

phrases.english: His mother?
She was מרים, who braided women's hair!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that his mother's name was סטדא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His mother's known name was מרים, so סטדא cannot be her name.

steps.title: סטדא is a nickname
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that סטדא is not a real name but a nickname, as people in פומבדיתא say: 'This one strayed from her husband.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As they say in פומבדיתא: 'סטת דא' — this one strayed from her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question: סטדא was a nickname for his mother, not her real name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her real name was מרים, but people called her סטדא, a play on the words 'סטת דא', meaning 'this one strayed.' This explains every name without any clash.

keyTerms.meaning: A major Torah town in Babylonia

steps.whatToRemember: בן סטדא is named after a nickname of his mother (מרים), from 'סטת דא', 'she strayed from her husband.'
steps.confusionAlert: סטדא is not anyone's real name here. It is a nickname, which is why the earlier answers kept running into the real names.

phrases.english: As they say in פומבדיתא:
"This one strayed from her husband."
phrases.notes: The words 'סטת דא' sound like 'סטדא', so the nickname comes from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 20 and closes the discussion about the name.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: סטדא was taken as someone's real name.
steps.terutzMaskana: סטדא is a nickname for the mother, meaning 'she strayed.'

steps.title: משנה: who is the מדיח
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה defines the מדיח as someone who says, 'Let us go and worship idols.'
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The מדיח is the one who says: 'Let us go and worship idols.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains who counts as a מדיח, one of the people who get סקילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (step 10), רב said the מדיח is someone who leads a whole city astray. Here the משנה gives his words: 'Let us go and worship idols,' said to a group.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who leads a group or city astray

phrases.english: משנה:
The מדיח: this is one who says:
"Let us go and worship idols."

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּדִּיחַ – זֶה הָאוֹמֵר: נֵלֵךְ וְנַעֲבוֹד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of the מסית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מדיח is one who says, 'Let us go and worship idols.'

steps.title: Only real sorcery makes a sorcerer liable
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds the מכשף to the list of those stoned, and limits it to someone who does a real act, not someone who only fools the eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sorcerer is stoned. Someone who does a real act of sorcery is liable, but not someone who only tricks people's eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of those who get stoning and now adds the מכשף. It defines who counts: only a person who does real sorcery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of 'sorcerers.' One actually does something through sorcery. The other only makes it look as if something happened, like a magic trick. Only the first one is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: One who performs a real act (of sorcery)
Literally 'grabs the eyes': fools people with an illusion

steps.confusionAlert: The illusionist is not punished by this משנה, but that does not mean what he does is fine. The משנה only says he is not liable to this death penalty.

phrases.english: The sorcerer [is also among those stoned].
One who performs a real act is liable,
but not one who deceives the eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of those stoned, moving from the מדיח to the מכשף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one who performs real sorcery is liable; one who only creates an illusion is not.

steps.title: The two cucumber gatherers
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא, in the name of רבי יהושע, shows the difference with an example: two people gather cucumbers by sorcery, and one is liable while the other is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says in the name of רבי יהושע: Two people gather cucumbers. One is exempt and one is liable. The one who did a real act is liable. The one who only fooled the eyes is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא brings a real-life example to show the rule from the last step. Two people seem to do the same thing, but only one is punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the outside, both people look like they gathered cucumbers by sorcery. The difference is what really happened. One really did it through sorcery, and the other only created an illusion.
steps.whyThisMatters: The example shows that the law looks at what actually happened, not at how things looked to people watching.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:
Two people gather cucumbers,
phrases.notes: He means they gather them through sorcery, not by hand.

phrases.english: one gathers and is exempt,
and one gathers and is liable.
The one who performs a real act is liable,
the one who deceives the eyes is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a concrete example of the rule just stated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two people can appear to do the same sorcery; the real one is liable and the illusionist is exempt.

steps.title: The משנה's מדיח includes those who lead a whole city astray
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens. רב יהודה quotes רב that the משנה's case of the מדיח is talking about those who lead an עיר הנדחת astray.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The משנה here is teaching about those who lead an idolatrous city astray.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and goes back to the משנה's line about the מדיח from step 22. רב explains which case the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the מדיח in the משנה is only a person who pushes individuals to worship idols. רב says the משנה is talking about those who lead a whole city astray. So both kinds get the same punishment, stoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who lead a whole city to worship idols
'They taught here': this is the case the משנה means

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
They taught here the subverters of an idolatrous city.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב מַדִּיחֵי עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת שָׁנוּ כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Skips past the מכשף and returns to clarify the מדיח from step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's מדיח includes those who lead an entire city to idolatry; they too are stoned.

steps.title: מכשפה includes both men and women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the מכשף and quotes a ברייתא: the פסוק's word מכשפה covers both a man and a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The sorcerer is one who performs an act, etc.' The Sages taught: 'A witch' means both a man and a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about the מכשף and brings a ברייתא about the פסוק. The ברייתא says the law covers men and women alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses a female word, מכשפה, a witch. Someone could think only women are included. The ברייתא says no: men are included too.

keyTerms.meaning: Witch: the female form used in the פסוק
Both a man and a woman

phrases.english: The sorcerer is one who performs a real act, etc.
The Sages taught:
'A witch' means both a man and a woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְכַשֵּׁף זֶה הָעוֹשֶׂה מַעֲשֶׂה וְכוּ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens discussion of the מכשף part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The law of מכשפה applies to men and women equally.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say 'witch'?
steps.stepSummary: If men are included too, why does the פסוק use the female word?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the verse say 'witch'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a natural question about what it just said. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the law covers men and women, the תורה could have used a general word. The female word looks like it needs a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What does the verse come to teach?': why is this wording used?

phrases.english: If so, why does the verse state 'a witch'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the פסוק in light of the ruling just made.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the פסוק uses the female form if men are included.

steps.title: Most women were involved in sorcery
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק uses the female word because it speaks about the common case: most women were familiar with sorcery.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because most women are commonly involved in sorcery.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. The פסוק describes the usual case, but the law is the same for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The female word does not limit the law. It only reflects who usually did sorcery back then. The תורה speaks about the common case.
steps.whatToRemember: The word מכשפה is female only because the תורה speaks about the common case. Any man or woman who does real sorcery is included.

phrases.english: Because most women are familiar with witchcraft.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the female wording.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק speaks about the common case, since most women were involved in sorcery.

steps.title: How are sorcerers put to death?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks which death penalty is given to sorcerers.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what are they put to death?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens: which kind of death penalty does a sorcerer get? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'do not let a witch live' but does not say how to carry out the death penalty. So the ברייתא has to find the method.

keyTerms.meaning: With what is their death carried out?

phrases.english: In what manner is their death carried out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who counts as a מכשפה to how a מכשפה is punished.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which death penalty applies to a sorcerer.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: by the sword, from matching words
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי links 'do not let a witch live' to 'do not let anything that breathes live.' The Canaanite nations in that second פסוק were killed by the sword, so a sorcerer is killed by the sword.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: Here it says 'Do not let a witch live,' and there it says 'Do not let anything that breathes live.' Just as there it is by the sword, so too here it is by the sword.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי answers by connecting two פסוקים that both use the words 'do not let live' (לא תחיה). He learns the method of death from the other פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the same words, לא תחיה. The second פסוק is about the Canaanite nations, who were killed by the sword. So he says the sorcerer is also killed by the sword. This seems to differ from the משנה, which lists the מכשף among those who are stoned.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It says here... and it says there': links two פסוקים with the same words
Learning a law from matching words in two פסוקים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the משנה. The משנה puts the מכשף in the list of those stoned, while רבי יוסי הגלילי here says the sword.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a matching phrase in two different פסוקים can carry a law from one place to another.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
It is stated here: 'Do not let a witch live,'
and it is stated there: 'Do not let anything that breathes live.'
Just as there it is by the sword,
so too here it is by the sword.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר נֶאֱמַר כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about how a sorcerer is executed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Through the shared words לא תחיה, the sorcerer is killed by the sword, like the Canaanite nations.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא says a sorcerer is stoned
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא compares 'do not let a witch live' to the פסוק about touching הר סיני, 'whether animal or man, it shall not live.' That case is stoning, so a מכשף is stoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: Here it says 'Do not let a witch live,' and there it says 'Whether animal or man, it shall not live.' Just as there it means stoning, here too it means stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי. He gives his own comparison, which leads to stoning instead of the sword.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same method: find another פסוק with the words 'not live' and borrow its death penalty. רבי עקיבא picks the פסוק about הר סיני, which talks about stoning. So for him a מכשף gets סקילה, not סייף.

keyTerms.meaning: Stoning, one of the four death penalties of בית דין
There, in the other פסוק being compared
Just as there, so too here. This is the formula for borrowing a law from one פסוק to another.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
It is said here: "Do not let a witch live,"
and it is said there:
"Whether animal or man, it shall not live."
phrases.notes: שמות 19:13. This is about touching הר סיני, and that same פסוק says the person 'shall be stoned.'

phrases.english: Just as there it is by stoning,
so too here it is by stoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing answer to the question in step 29, against רבי יוסי הגלילי's answer in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מכשף is killed by סקילה, learned from the הר סיני פסוק.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: my words match better than yours
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי points out that his comparison uses the exact same word, 'לא תחיה,' while רבי עקיבא's uses a different form, 'לא יחיה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to him: I learned 'do not let live' from 'do not let live,' but you learned 'do not let live' from 'it shall not live'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי attacks רבי עקיבא's comparison. He says his own word match is closer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison between פסוקים is stronger when the words are exactly the same. רבי יוסי's two פסוקים both say 'לא תחיה,' while רבי עקיבא's other פסוק says 'לא יחיה.' So רבי יוסי claims his source should win.

keyTerms.meaning: I learned, I derived (a law from a comparison)
Do not let live (you must not keep alive)
It shall not live (a different form of the same root)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to him:
I learned "do not let live" from "do not let live,"
but you learned "do not let live" from "it shall not live"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison רבי עקיבא made in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's comparison of 'לא תחיה' to 'לא יחיה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words in רבי עקיבא's comparison are not the same, while רבי יוסי's are identical. An exact match should be stronger.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: I compare Jews to Jews
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that his comparison is from Jews to Jews, who have many kinds of death penalties. רבי יוסי compares Jews to non-Jews, who have only a limited set.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: I learned about Jews from Jews, for whom the תורה gave many kinds of death penalties. You learned about Jews from non-Jews, for whom the תורה gave only...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא defends his comparison. He says the topic match matters more than the exact word match. His sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הר סיני פסוק is about Jews, just like the מכשף law. Jews have several death penalties, so a פסוק that picks stoning for them is a meaningful choice. רבי יוסי's פסוק about the sword is about non-Jewish nations, which have far fewer kinds of death penalty, so it fits less well.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah gave them many (here: many kinds of death penalty)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא does not deny that רבי יוסי's words match better. He argues that matching the topic (Jews to Jews) is more important than matching the exact word.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
I learned about Jews from Jews,
for whom the Torah gave many kinds of death penalties,
and you learned about Jews from non-Jews,
for whom the Torah gave only...
